precepts.text: In a great house there are vessels of gold, silver, wood, and earth; that house is the house of Israel.
precepts.point: The waters that issue out from under the threshold are the word of the Most High. Just as a tub fills when the water is left running, the word is now being issued out to the four corners of the earth.

note.label: Ezekiel 47: The Waters Issuing from the House

precepts.why:
Ezekiel speaks by similitude and dark sayings, so the house the waters issue from is not a literal building. Paul says, “in a great house there are not only vessels of gold and of silver, but also of wood and of earth; and some to honour, and some to dishonour.”

That great house, with its vessels of gold, silver, wood and earth, is the house of Israel. The house here in Ezekiel is that spiritual house, the house of Israel, and the waters that issue out from under its threshold eastward are the word of the Most High going out.

precepts.text: We as lively stones are built up a spiritual house; this spiritual house represents Israel.
precepts.point: The waters that issue out from under the threshold are the word of the Most High. Just as a tub fills when the water is left running, the word is now being issued out to the four corners of the earth.

note.label: Ezekiel 47: The Waters Issuing from the House

precepts.why:
“Ye also, as lively stones, are built up a spiritual house, an holy priesthood, to offer up spiritual sacrifices, acceptable to God by Jesus Christ.” We, as lively stones, are built up a spiritual house. That spiritual house represents Israel.

So the house whose threshold the waters come from under, whose forefront stands toward the east, is the house of Israel, not a literal building. Ezekiel speaks by similitude and dark sayings, and the waters coming down from under the right side of the house, at the south side of the altar, are the word of the Most High issuing out.

precepts.text: He sanctifies and cleanses it with the washing of water by the word; the water here represents the word.
precepts.point: The waters that issue out from under the threshold are the word of the Most High. Just as a tub fills when the water is left running, the word is now being issued out to the four corners of the earth.

note.label: Ezekiel 47: The Waters Issuing from the House

precepts.why:
The waters are the word. Christ sanctifies and cleanses the church “with the washing of water by the word”. The water here represents the word of the Most High.

So the “waters issued out from under the threshold of the house eastward” are the word issuing out of the spiritual house, the house of Israel. Just as a tub fills when the water is left running, the word is now being issued out to the four corners of the earth.

precepts.text: My doctrine shall drop as the rain; the doctrine of the Most High is the water now distilling to every corner like dew.
precepts.point: The waters that issue out from under the threshold are the word of the Most High. Just as a tub fills when the water is left running, the word is now being issued out to the four corners of the earth.

note.label: Ezekiel 47: The Waters Issuing from the House

precepts.why:
Moses says, “My doctrine shall drop as the rain, my speech shall distil as the dew, as the small rain upon the tender herb, and as the showers upon the grass: Because I will publish the name of the Lord”. The doctrine of the Most High is water: it drops as rain and distils as dew.

That is the water issuing out from under the threshold of the house, the word of the Most High. The doctrine is now distilling to every corner like dew; as a tub fills when the water is left running, the word is being issued out to the four corners of the earth, publishing the name of the Lord.

precepts.text: For I give you good doctrine, forsake ye not my law; the doctrines are the laws.
precepts.point: The waters that issue out from under the threshold are the word of the Most High. Just as a tub fills when the water is left running, the word is now being issued out to the four corners of the earth.

note.label: Ezekiel 47: The Waters Issuing from the House

precepts.why:
“For I give you good doctrine, forsake ye not my law.” The doctrines are the laws. Good doctrine and the law are the same thing in the same breath.

So when Moses says his doctrine shall drop as the rain, and the water issuing from the house is the word, that water is the law of the Most High. The word going out from the spiritual house of Israel to the four corners of the earth is His good doctrine, His law, and we are not to forsake it.

precepts.text: He gave apostles, prophets, evangelists, pastors and teachers, till we all come unto the measure of the stature of the fulness of Christ.
precepts.point: The measuring line measures us up to the stature of Christ, the understanding of the laws and the doctrines.

note.label: Ezekiel 47: The Waters Issuing from the House

precepts.why:
The man with the line measures a thousand cubits and the waters are to the ankles; a thousand more, to the knees; a thousand more, to the loins; then a river that cannot be passed over, “waters to swim in”. The rising water is the word being preached and the understanding increasing as it goes to the four corners of the earth: people coming to understand that Christ is a black man, that we are the Israelites, and that we must keep the commandments.

The measuring line measures us up to the stature of Christ. He “gave some, apostles; and some, prophets; and some, evangelists; and some, pastors and teachers; For the perfecting of the saints, for the work of the ministry, for the edifying of the body of Christ: Till we all come in the unity of the faith, and of the knowledge of the Son of God, unto a perfect man, unto the measure of the stature of the fulness of Christ”. That measure is the understanding of the laws and the doctrines.

It comes in stages, ankles, knees, loins, just as understanding came out over time in the classes: the head covering out of First Corinthians 11, the sabbath, and the new moon being the full moon around 2006 to 2007. As long as we stay in the spirit, more revelation will keep coming, until the water is a river to swim in.

precepts.text: I will send you Elijah the prophet, and he shall turn the heart of the fathers to the children before the great and dreadful day.
precepts.point: Because we now understand who we are and can identify our forefathers in this Bible, it means Elijah has already come and gone.

note.label: Ezekiel 47: The Waters Issuing from the House

precepts.why:
“Son of man, hast thou seen this?” He brings the prophet back to the brink of the river, and there are very many trees on the one side and on the other. Malachi says, “Behold, I will send you Elijah the prophet before the coming of the great and dreadful day of the Lord: And he shall turn the heart of the fathers to the children, and the heart of the children to their fathers, lest I come and smite the earth with a curse.”

Elijah's work is to turn the heart of the children to their fathers. Because we now understand who we are and can identify our forefathers in this Bible, our hearts have been turned to our fathers. That means Elijah has already come and gone, before the great and dreadful day.

precepts.text: Keep my commandments, and live; life comes through keeping the law.
precepts.point: We receive life through the commandments.

note.label: Ezekiel 47: The Waters Issuing from the House

precepts.why:
The waters go toward the east country, down into the desert and into the sea, and the waters are healed: “every thing that liveth, which moveth, whithersoever the rivers shall come, shall live”. Life comes wherever the river comes.

The river is the word, and “Keep my commandments, and live; and my law as the apple of thine eye.” We receive life through the commandments. Life comes through keeping the law, so wherever the word of the Most High reaches and is kept, every thing shall live.

precepts.text: Follow me, and I will make you fishers of men; the fishers point to the same last-day gathering of Israel.
precepts.point: The fishers stand upon it from Engedi to Eneglaim, and the fish are according to their kinds, exceeding many. This is Israel in the last days coming alive again and growing into an exceeding great army.

note.label: Ezekiel 47: The Waters Issuing from the House

precepts.why:
“the fishers shall stand upon it from En–gedi even unto En–eglaim”, a place to spread forth nets, and “their fish shall be according to their kinds, as the fish of the great sea, exceeding many.” Christ said to His disciples, “Follow me, and I will make you fishers of men.”

The fishers are fishers of men, and the fish exceeding many, according to their kinds, are Israel in the last days coming alive again and growing into an exceeding great army. The fishers on the river of the word point to that same last-day gathering of Israel.

precepts.text: Bring forth fruits meet for repentance, for the axe is laid to the root of every tree that does not.
precepts.point: The tree represents Israel, and once the word spreads we know how to bring forth fruit.

note.label: Ezekiel 47: The Waters Issuing from the House

precepts.why:
By the river grow “all trees for meat, whose leaf shall not fade, neither shall the fruit thereof be consumed”, bringing forth new fruit according to their months, “because their waters they issued out of the sanctuary”. The tree represents Israel, and its fruit comes from the water, the word.

“Bring forth therefore fruits meet for repentance”. The axe is laid to the root of every tree that does not. Once the word spreads, we know how to bring forth fruit: fruits meet for repentance, new fruit every month, leaf that does not fade, because our waters issued out of the sanctuary.

precepts.text: Thou shouldest not have looked on the day of thy brother in the day that he became a stranger; a stranger is one living out of his own land among his tribesmen.
precepts.point: The stranger here is not another nation. A stranger is an Israelite living out of his own tribe's land; if you are of Judah and you sojourn in Benjamin, you are counted a stranger. Christianity uses this verse to claim the other nations dwell among Israel and receive the land, but that is not what is being said.

note.label: Ezekiel 47: The Waters Issuing from the House

precepts.why:
“the strangers that sojourn among you” who get inheritance among the tribes of Israel are not another nation. Obadiah shows what a stranger is: “thou shouldest not have looked on the day of thy brother in the day that he became a stranger; neither shouldest thou have rejoiced over the children of Judah in the day of their destruction”.

Judah became a stranger in the day of their destruction, when they were put out of their own land. A stranger is one living out of his own land, an Israelite out of his own tribe's land among his tribesmen. If you are of Judah and you sojourn in Benjamin, you are counted a stranger, and “in what tribe the stranger sojourneth, there shall ye give him his inheritance”.

Christianity uses this verse to claim the other nations dwell among Israel and receive the land, but that is not what is being said. The stranger is thy brother.

precepts.text: Israel dwelt as strangers away from their own land, showing what a stranger is.
precepts.point: The stranger here is not another nation. A stranger is an Israelite living out of his own tribe's land; if you are of Judah and you sojourn in Benjamin, you are counted a stranger. Christianity uses this verse to claim the other nations dwell among Israel and receive the land, but that is not what is being said.

note.label: Ezekiel 47: The Waters Issuing from the House

precepts.why:
“And these are they of Jewry that came up from the captivity, where they dwelt as strangers, whom Nabuchodonosor the king of Babylon had carried away unto Babylon.” Israel dwelt as strangers in Babylon, away from their own land. That is what a stranger is: an Israelite living out of his own land.

So the stranger that sojourns among you and begets children, counted “as born in the country among the children of Israel” and given inheritance in the tribe where he sojourns, is an Israelite out of his own tribe's land. Of Judah, sojourning in Benjamin, you are the stranger. It is not another nation receiving the land, whatever Christianity claims from this verse.

Those being sealed are not only this generation. Generations before us knew this knowledge, not to the level we have now. This deals with time and understanding. “Behold, waters issued out from under the threshold of the house eastward”: the waters are the word of God.

“He measured a thousand cubits, and he brought me through the waters; the waters were to the ankles.” The understanding of the word of God was only to the ankles. “Again he measured a thousand, and brought me through the waters; the waters were to the knees”: the understanding of God’s laws came to the knees. Then to the loins. When I came in as a youth, the only law we kept was the beard law; we fellowshipped on the sabbath but still cooked on the sabbath, still bought and sold on the sabbath, and the women wore a dress one day a week.

“And it was a river that I could not pass over: for the waters were risen, waters to swim in”: a time will come when the word of God will fill the earth. Our ancestors who preceded us weren’t where we are today, and the Most High is going to judge them based on the understanding they had at that time, not the same understanding the brothers have today, because it wasn’t open to them.
The precept for the pure river: “And, behold, waters issued out from under the threshold of the house eastward.”
“Open thou mine eyes, that I may behold wondrous things out of thy law”: this is why we ask the Lord to open our understanding when we pray.

Saying the same thing as David: “The eyes of your understanding being enlightened”: our spiritual eyes being opened. We are in darkness now, the season of night, and we ask the Lord to open our eyes so we can better guide the people, ourselves and our families.
The trees on the sides of the river: “And he shall be like a tree planted by the rivers of water, that bringeth forth his fruit in his season.”

The healing of the nations. “Every one that is left of all the nations which came against Jerusalem”: the nations not destroyed when Christ returns; there will be a lot of people left, to pay for their judgment and serve. “Shall even go up from year to year to worship the King, the Lord of hosts, and to keep the feast of tabernacles.” “Even upon them shall be no rain”: no rain means drought; the plants don’t grow, the cattle can’t eat, and you die. Everyone will celebrate God’s high holy days, or they will die.

“From one new moon to another, and from one sabbath to another, shall all flesh come to worship before me”: everybody on the planet will honour the Sabbath and the new moon. You won’t be celebrating Halloween or Kwanzaa ever again.
This whole chapter is a parable. “I am not sent but unto the lost sheep of the house of Israel.”

Christ’s parable of us as fishers: “The kingdom of heaven is like unto a net, that was cast into the sea, and gathered of every kind.” “And gathered the good into vessels, but cast the bad away”: this Bible is like a net. We go out and teach, and people come in. What if another nation comes in, or someone’s great-great-grandfather was an Edomite? “The angels shall come forth, and sever the wicked from among the just.” Don’t worry about it; the angels will separate them.

“From whence then hath it tares?”: some look like Israel but they are not; they are tares, the other nations. “Wilt thou then that we go and gather them up? But he said, Nay; lest while ye gather up the tares, ye root up also the wheat with them”: we could make a mistake through visuals and rip up an Israelite thinking he is another nation.

The miry places that shall not be healed. The feet and toes are the last kingdom on earth, America and the European Union. “The kingdom shall be divided; but there shall be in it of the strength of the iron”: the iron represents the military. “They shall mingle themselves with the seed of men”: the miry clay represents the mixed multitude of this kingdom. “And in the days of these kings shall the God of heaven set up a kingdom”: Israel United in Christ growing is the beginning of the kingdom. “And the kingdom shall not be left to other people”: the kingdom of heaven is not for other nations. “And the dream is certain”: it shall surely come to pass. This is the last empire on earth; we don’t have time for going off.

“For the controversy of Zion”: who the land of Israel belongs to and who the twelve tribes really are. “And the land thereof shall become burning pitch”: those are the miry places. “From generation to generation it shall lie waste”: there will be no healing for this place.

Officers set over the nations: “Because thou hast been faithful in a very little, have thou authority over ten cities.” The very little is the understanding we have today. New York alone is about eight million people, and to make them obey the word of God we need power. On the other side, over ten cities, you will have a regiment of men under you to make sure the dietary law and the dress code are obeyed. When the white man took over, he changed our language and made sure we never called ourselves Israelites again; when we are set over the cities, they won’t call themselves Chinese ever again. They go back to the God-given name: Moab.

“And every tree, in the which is the fruit of a tree yielding seed; to you it shall be for meat”: that was Adam’s diet, the diet of everybody on the planet before the flood, animals included. We won’t be eating chicken; on Passover we might have lamb or goat.

The knowledge of herbs. “For he hath given me certain knowledge of the things that are, namely, to know how the world was made, and the operation of the elements”: Solomon was on such a high level of understanding. “The beginning, ending, and midst of the times”: he saw the whole spectrum. “The alterations of the turning of the sun”: the Bible says the sun goes around the earth. “The natures of living creatures, and the furies of wild beasts”: Esau tags animals and puts cameras on them, but Solomon already knew. “And the reasonings of men”: he understood why you did the evil you did. “The diversities of plants and the virtues of roots”: we are going to get that understanding.

“And the gates of the city shall be after the names of the tribes of Israel.” “And one gate of Joseph, one gate of Benjamin, one gate of Dan”: the gate of Dan is not recorded in Revelation 7. That is why chapters 47 and 48 go into when we returned from the Persian captivity and had to divide the land.

points: The waters issuing from under the threshold of the house eastward is the vision behind what John saw.
Ankles, knees, loins, then waters to swim in: that is the progression of how this truth came in and grew.
The water is risen so high now it cannot be passed over. You cannot get around us, and every one of you can answer for your faith.
The trees standing on both banks of the river are the same trees John saw.
The fruit is for meat and the leaf for medicine, and those waters came out of the sanctuary: the laws of God.
The waters go into the sea and the sea is healed: this word is going through America, Africa, Asia Minor, Europe, Arabia and down to Australia.

The man with the line went forth eastward and measured, and the waters that ran out on the right side going out from the temple is the gospel going out, the man with the line measuring your understanding of the scriptures.

points: “Behold, there ran out waters on the right side”: he is looking at a vision of the temple, and he sees waters gushing out from all sides of it.

“And when the man that had the line in his hand went forth eastward”: the line is a measuring instrument, and the man is an angel taking Ezekiel by the hand. “The waters were to the ankles”: Ezekiel 47 deals with time. When the truth first started to come out, the people’s understanding was only at the ankles. In the sixties the Israelites weren’t really keeping the Sabbath; they were still buying and selling and cooking on it, and the women dressed like women only on the Sabbath day.

“The waters were to the knees”: time has gone by, and the understanding of scripture has risen. “The waters were to the loins”: time has passed on and the waters have risen. Some camps never kept the new moon, or Tabernacles, until the Lord showed us in the law, and now people are mad because the Lord is using us.

“And it was a river that I could not pass over: for the waters were risen, waters to swim in”: the word of God covered the earth. It wasn’t at the ankles, the knees or the loins any more; it covered the entire globe.

“Then he brought me, and caused me to return to the brink of the river”: the angel brought him back to the bank to explain. “Behold, at the bank of the river were very many trees on the one side and on the other”: the trees in the garden in Genesis were people, and that is what this parable goes into. These trees are the man embedded in the word of God, Psalms 1:3.

“Which being brought forth into the sea, the waters shall be healed. And it shall come to pass, that every thing that liveth, which moveth, whithersoever the rivers shall come, shall live”: everywhere the word of God touches and they are obedient to it, they shall live. That is the leaves of the tree for the healing of the nations in Revelation 22.

“And it shall come to pass, that the fishers shall stand upon it”: in verse 7 we were trees, now we are fishers; Christ said I will make you fishers of men. “Their fish shall be according to their kinds”: we are not fishing for other nations. “As the fish of the great sea, exceeding many”: Israel cannot be measured nor numbered.
When black people go off into sin, remember Daniel in Susanna calling the wicked elders the seed of Canaan and not of Judah. Judge not according to the appearance, but judge righteous judgment.

“But the miry places thereof and the marishes thereof shall not be healed; they shall be given to salt”: every sacrifice is seasoned with salt. The miry places are this place, which will never be healed.

“And by the river upon the bank thereof, on this side and on that side, shall grow all trees for meat, whose leaf shall not fade, neither shall the fruit thereof be consumed”: the fruit is understanding. When the Passover, the feast of unleavened bread or the Sabbath comes, everybody must obey, and to obey means you will be healed in your land. Moab in their land must obey the commandments of God to be healed, and we will have officers set there to ensure everybody obeys.

It is twofold: it is talking about the actual fruit we will eat, but more so it goes into the word of the Most High. “And the leaf thereof for medicine”: the scriptures as well as the literal understanding of herbs.

Verse 13 down through chapter 48 is about the division of the land. Ezekiel was in the Babylonian captivity, under the Cushites. In the Persian and Median captivity the king of Persia let us go and build the temple again, as you read in Ezra, Nehemiah and Haggai. When we got back to the land we had to divide it according to the tribes of Israel and rebuild the temple according to Exodus and Numbers. That is what Ezekiel 47:13 through 48 is about, along with us sacrificing again.
